system: You are a security investigator reviewing an alert. Base every claim only on the evidence available to you. Cite the record IDs that support each observation.

supporting_observations.claim: Five interactive logon attempts for leo.martins failed on WS-LMARTINS-01 between 13:30:32 and 13:30:56 UTC; each reports an incorrect password.
After two failed network logons for leo.martins, the domain controller recorded a successful network logon for the account from 203.0.113.250 at 13:48:06 UTC.

The successful network logon from 203.0.113.250 is inconsistent with the supplied environment context that there is no VPN and remote administration is only performed from WS-SOKAFOR-01; this makes the success suspicious.

A few minutes later, the domain controller issued a Kerberos ticket for leo.martins from 10.40.10.23 to WS-NBLAKE-01, followed by a successful network logon for the account on WS-NBLAKE-01 from that address.

The external-address success and subsequent authentication to WS-NBLAKE-01 warrant investigation as potentially unauthorized account use; the records do not establish that these events share the same actor or session.

WS-LMARTINS-01 recorded ordinary-looking user activity, including Explorer registry updates and a proxy connection to www.bing.com; this does not explain or validate the successful network logon from 203.0.113.250.

known_telemetry_limitations: The DC event records the source address and a successful network logon, but the provided logs do not identify the remote client device or the resource accessed.
The records do not link the external-address logon, the later WS-NBLAKE-01 authentication, and local activity on WS-LMARTINS-01 to one session or actor.
The address 203.0.113.250 is in a documentation-only address range; it may be sanitized, so its real-world ownership or routability cannot be determined from these records.
The supplied window contains selected events, not complete authentication, endpoint, network, or account-change telemetry.
claims_not_established: Whether the successful logon from 203.0.113.250 was authorized or whether the address represents a sanitized value.
Whether the successful network logon was initiated by leo.martins, an attacker, or an intermediary.
Whether the later WS-NBLAKE-01 authentication was legitimate help-desk activity or related to the external-address logon.
Whether any data was accessed, copied, or exfiltrated, or whether the account or hosts were otherwise compromised.
additional_evidence_needed: Validate the source address against firewall, NAT, DHCP, proxy, and network flow records, accounting for possible log sanitization.
Review complete DC authentication and account-change events around the time, including source workstation details and any related successful or failed logons.
Collect endpoint logon-session, process, and network telemetry from WS-LMARTINS-01 and WS-NBLAKE-01 around the relevant events.
Confirm with leo.martins and the help desk whether the logons and activity were expected; verify any applicable remote-access or exception records.
Review access to resources following the successful logons and investigate for unauthorized changes or data access.
